chapter.li: LEChapter1 Verse1 Paul, an apostle, a servant of God (called of Jesus Christ) and separated to preach the gospel VerseEnd Verse2 which he had promised before by his prophets in the holy scriptures VerseEnd Verse3 concerning his Son Jesus Christ, our Lord, who was made of the seed of David according to the flesh VerseEnd Verse4 and declared the Son of God with power by the spirit — according to the truth, through the resurrection from the dead VerseEnd — Verse5 by whom we have received grace and apostleship, through obedience and faith on his name, to preach the gospel among all nations, VerseEnd Verse6 among whom you also are called of Jesus Christ. VerseEnd Verse7 Wherefore, I write to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called saints: Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. VerseEnd

Verse8 First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ that you all are steadfast, and your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world. VerseEnd Verse9 For God is my witness, whom I serve, that without ceasing I make mention of you always in my prayers, that you may be kept through the spirit in the gospel of his Son. VerseEnd Verse10 Making request of you to remember me in your prayers, I now write unto you that you will ask him in faith, that if by any means at length I may serve you with my labors and may have a prosperous journey by the will of God to come unto you. VerseEnd Verse11 For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, that it may be established in you to the end, VerseEnd Verse12 that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me. VerseEnd

Verse13 Now I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that oftentimes I purposed to come unto you — but was hindered hitherto — that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles. VerseEnd Verse14 I am debtor both to the Greeks and to the foreigners, both to the wise and to the unwise. VerseEnd Verse15 And as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you that are at Rome also. VerseEnd Verse16 For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ, for it is the power of God unto salvation to everyone that believes — to the Jew first, and also to the Greek; VerseEnd Verse17 for therein is the righteousness of God revealed through faith on his name, as it is written: The just shall live by faith. VerseEnd

Verse18 For the wrath of God is revealed from Heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men who love not the truth, but remain in unrighteousness VerseEnd Verse19 after that which may be known of God is manifest to them. VerseEnd Verse20 For God has revealed unto them the invisible things of him, from the creation of the world, which are clearly seen — things which are not seen being understood by the things that are made through his eternal power and Godhead — so that they are without excuse; VerseEnd Verse21 because when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were they thankful, but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish hearts were darkened. VerseEnd Verse22 Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools VerseEnd Verse23 and changed the glory of the incorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and four-footed beasts, and creeping things. VerseEnd Verse24 Wherefore, God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonor their own bodies between themselves, VerseEnd Verse25 who changed the truth of God into a lie and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. VerseEnd

Verse26 For this cause, God gave them up unto vile affections; for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature; VerseEnd Verse27 and likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another — men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompense of their error which was meet. VerseEnd

Verse28 And even as they did not like to retain God according to some knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not proper VerseEnd — Verse29 being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, VerseEnd Verse30 backbiters, haters of God, insolent, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, VerseEnd Verse31 without understanding, covenant breakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful. VerseEnd Verse32 And some who — knowing the judgment of God, that they who commit such things are worthy of death — are inexcusable not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them. VerseEnd

LEChapter2 Verse1 Therefore, you are inexcusable, O man, whoever you are, that thus judges; for wherein you judge another, you condemn yourself — for you who judges does the same things. VerseEnd Verse2 But we are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them who commit such things. VerseEnd Verse3 And do you think this, O man who judges them who do such things and does the same: that you shall escape the judgment of God? VerseEnd

Verse4 Or do you despise the riches of his goodness, and tolerance, and long-suffering, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance? VerseEnd Verse5 But after your hardness and impenitent heart, treasure up unto yourself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God, VerseEnd Verse6 who will render to every man according to his deeds. VerseEnd Verse7 To them who by patient continuance in well-doing seek for glory, and honor, and immortality: eternal life; VerseEnd Verse8 but unto them that are contentious and do not obey the truth but obey unrighteousness: indignation and wrath, VerseEnd Verse9 tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that does evil — of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile. VerseEnd Verse10 But glory, honor, and peace to every man that works good — to the Jew first, and also to the Gentile; VerseEnd Verse11 for there is no respect of persons with God. VerseEnd

Verse12 For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law. And as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law, VerseEnd Verse13 for the hearers of the law are not just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified VerseEnd — Verse14 for when the Gentiles, who have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves, VerseEnd Verse15 who show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the meanwhile accusing or else excusing one another, VerseEnd Verse16 in the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ, according to the gospel. VerseEnd

Verse17 Behold, you are called a Jew, and rest in the law, and make your boast of God, VerseEnd Verse18 and know his will, and approve the things that are more excellent, being instructed out of the law, VerseEnd Verse19 and are confident that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light of them who are in darkness, VerseEnd Verse20 an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, who has the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law. VerseEnd Verse21 You therefore who teach another, do you not teach yourself? You that preach a man should not steal, do you steal? VerseEnd Verse22 You that say a man should not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You that abhor idols, do you commit sacrilege? VerseEnd Verse23 You that make your boast of the law, through breaking the law do you dishonor God? VerseEnd Verse24 For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you, as it is written. VerseEnd

Verse25 For circumcision truly profits if you keep the law, but if you are a breaker of the law, your circumcision is made uncircumcision. VerseEnd Verse26 Therefore, if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision? VerseEnd Verse27 And shall not uncircumcision, which is by nature, if it fulfill the law, judge you who by the letter and circumcision does transgress the law? VerseEnd Verse28 For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision which is outward in the flesh. VerseEnd Verse29 But he is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is that of the heart — in the spirit and not in the letter — whose praise is not of men, but of God. VerseEnd

LEChapter3 Verse1 What advantage then has the Jew over the Gentile? Or what profit of circumcision, who is not a Jew from the heart? VerseEnd Verse2 But he who is a Jew from the heart I say has much every way, chiefly because unto them were committed the oracles of God. VerseEnd Verse3 For what if some did not believe? Shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect? VerseEnd Verse4 God forbid.

Yea, let God be true, but every man a liar, as it is written: that you might be justified in your sayings, and might overcome when you are judged. VerseEnd Verse5 But if we remain in our unrighteousness and commend the righteousness of God, how dare we say, God is unrighteous who takes vengeance. (I speak as a man who fears God. VerseEnd) Verse6 God forbid; for then how shall God judge the world? VerseEnd Verse7 For if the truth of God has more abounded through my lie — as it is called of the Jews — unto his glory, why yet am I also judged as a sinner, VerseEnd Verse8 and not received, because we are slanderously reported? And some affirm that we say (whose damnation is just), Let us do evil, that good may come. But this is false. VerseEnd

Verse9 If not so, what then? Are we better than they? No, by no means. For we have proved before that Jews and Gentiles are all under sin, VerseEnd Verse10 as it is written: There is none righteous, no, not one. VerseEnd Verse11 There is none that understands, there is none that seeks after God. VerseEnd Verse12 They have all gone out of the way, they have altogether become unprofitable; there is none that does good, no, not one. VerseEnd Verse13 Their throat is an open sepulcher; with their tongues, they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips VerseEnd Verse14 whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness; VerseEnd Verse15 their feet are swift to shed blood. VerseEnd Verse16 Destruction and misery are in their ways, VerseEnd Verse17 and the way of peace have they not known. VerseEnd Verse18 There is no fear of God before their eyes. VerseEnd

Verse19 Now we know that whatever things the law says, it says to them who are under the law, that every mouth may be stopped and all the world may become guilty before God; VerseEnd Verse20 for by the law is the knowledge of sin. Therefore, by the deeds of the law shall no flesh be justified in his sight. VerseEnd

Verse21 But now the righteousness of God apart from the law is manifested (being witnessed by the law and the prophets) VerseEnd, Verse22 even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ, unto all, and upon all them that believe — for there is no difference; VerseEnd Verse23 for all have sinned and come short of the glory of God, VerseEnd Verse24 therefore being justified only by his grace, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, VerseEnd Verse25 whom God has set forth to be a propitiation, through faith in his blood; to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the tolerance of God; to declare, VerseEnd Verse26 I say, at this time his righteousness, that he might be just, and the justifier of him who believes in Jesus. VerseEnd

Verse27 Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? Of works? Nay, but by the law of faith. VerseEnd Verse28 Therefore, we conclude that a man is justified alone by faith, apart from the deeds of the law. VerseEnd Verse29 Is he the God of the Jews only? Is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also, VerseEnd Verse30 seeing that God will justify the circumcision by faith and uncircumcision through faith. VerseEnd Verse31 Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid; yea, we establish the law. VerseEnd

LEChapter4 Verse1 What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, has found? VerseEnd Verse2 For if Abraham were justified by the law of works, he has to glory in himself, but not of God. VerseEnd Verse3 For what says the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. VerseEnd Verse4 Now to him who is justified by the law of works is the reward reckoned not of grace, but of debt. VerseEnd Verse5 But to him that seeks not to be justified by the law of works, but believes on him who justifies not the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness, VerseEnd Verse6 even as David also describes the blessedness of the man unto whom God imputes righteousness apart from the law of works, VerseEnd Verse7 saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven and whose sins are covered VerseEnd Verse8 through faith. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin. VerseEnd

Verse9 Does this blessedness then come upon the circumcised only? Or upon the uncircumcised also? For we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. VerseEnd Verse10 How was it then reckoned? When he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision. VerseEnd Verse11 And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had, yet being uncircumcised, that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised — that righteousness might be imputed unto them also VerseEnd — Verse12 and the father of circumcision to them who are not of the circumcision only, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had — being yet uncircumcised. VerseEnd Verse13 For the promise that he should be the heir of the world was not to Abraham or to his seed through the law, but through the righteousness of faith. VerseEnd Verse14 For if they who are of the law are heirs, faith is made void and the promise made of no effect, VerseEnd Verse15 because the law works wrath.

For where no law is, there is no transgression; VerseEnd Verse16 therefore, you are justified of faith and works through grace, to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed — not to them only who are of the law, but to them also who are of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all VerseEnd (Verse17 as it is written: I have made you a father of many nations) before him whom he believed — even God, who quickens the dead, and calls those things which are not as though they were VerseEnd — Verse18 who against hope believed in hope, that he might become the father of many nations according to that which was spoken: So shall your seed be. VerseEnd Verse19 And being not weak in faith, he considered not his own body now dead when he was about a hundred years old, neither yet the deadness of Sarah’s womb. VerseEnd Verse20 He hesitated not at the promise of God through unbelief, but was strong in faith, giving glory to God VerseEnd Verse21 and being fully persuaded that what he had promised, he was able also to perform, VerseEnd Verse22 and therefore it was imputed to him for righteousness. VerseEnd

Verse23 Now it was not written for his sake alone that it was imputed to him, VerseEnd Verse24 but for us also, to whom it shall be imputed if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead, VerseEnd Verse25 who was delivered for our offenses and was raised again for our justification. VerseEnd LEChapter5 Verse1 Therefore, being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, VerseEnd Verse2 by whom also we have access (by faith) into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God. VerseEnd

Verse3 And not only this, but we glory in tribulations also, knowing that tribulation works patience, VerseEnd Verse4 and patience, experience, and experience, hope. VerseEnd Verse5 And hope makes not ashamed, because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the holy ghost which is given unto us. VerseEnd Verse6 For when we were yet without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly. VerseEnd Verse7 For scarcely for a righteous man will one die, yet perhaps for a good man some would even dare to die. VerseEnd Verse8 But God commends his love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. VerseEnd Verse9 Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him; VerseEnd Verse10 for if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more (being reconciled) we shall be saved by his life. VerseEnd Verse11 And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement. VerseEnd

Verse12 Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin, and so death passed upon all men for all have sinned VerseEnd — Verse13 for before the law, sin was in the world — yet sin is not imputed to those who have no law. VerseEnd Verse14 Nevertheless, death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam’s transgression (who is the figure of him that was to come), for VerseEnd Verse15 I say that through the offense, death reigned over all. But the offense is not as the free gift, for the gift abounds; for if, through the offense of one, many are dead, much more the grace of God and the gift by grace has abounded by one man — Jesus Christ — unto many. VerseEnd Verse16 And not as it was by one that sinned, so is the gift — for the judgment is by one, to condemnation, but the free gift is of many offenses, unto justification; VerseEnd Verse17 for if by one man’s offense, death reigned by one, much more shall they who receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life by one — Jesus Christ. VerseEnd

Verse18 Therefore, as by the offense of one, judgment came upon all men to condemnation, even so by the righteousness of one, the free gift came upon all men unto justification of life. VerseEnd Verse19 For as by one man’s disobedience, many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous. VerseEnd Verse20 Moreover, the law entered that the offense might abound, but where sin abounded, grace did much more abound — VerseEnd Verse21 that as sin has reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life, by Jesus Christ our Lord. VerseEnd

LEChapter6 Verse1 What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin that grace may abound? VerseEnd Verse2 God forbid. How shall we, who are dead to sin, live any longer therein? VerseEnd Verse3 Do you not know that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death? VerseEnd Verse4 Therefore, we are buried with him by baptism into death, that like Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life. VerseEnd Verse5 For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection, VerseEnd Verse6 knowing this: that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin; VerseEnd Verse7 for he that is dead to sin is freed from sin. VerseEnd

Verse8 Now if we are dead with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him, VerseEnd Verse9 knowing that Christ, being raised from the dead, dies no more; death has no more dominion over him. VerseEnd Verse10 For in that he died, he died unto sin once; but in that he lives, he lives unto God. VerseEnd Verse11 Likewise, reckon also yourselves to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord. VerseEnd

Verse12 Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that you should obey it in the lusts thereof, VerseEnd Verse13 neither yield your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin. But yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God. VerseEnd Verse14 For in so doing, sin shall not have dominion over you, for you are not under the law, but under grace. VerseEnd

Verse15 What then? Shall we sin because we are not under the law but under grace? God forbid. VerseEnd Verse16 Do you not know that to whom you yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants you are to whom you obey? Whether of sin unto death or of obedience unto righteousness? VerseEnd Verse17 But God be thanked that you are not the servants of sin, for you have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you. VerseEnd Verse18 Being then made free from sin, you became the servants of righteousness. VerseEnd Verse19 I speak after the manner of men because of the infirmity of your flesh: for as you have yielded your members in times past servants to uncleanness and to iniquity, unto iniquity, even so now yield your members servants to righteousness, unto holiness. VerseEnd Verse20 For when you were the servants of sin, you were free from righteousness. VerseEnd Verse21 What fruit did you have then in those things whereof you are now ashamed? For the end of those things is death. VerseEnd Verse22 But now being made free from sin, and have become servants to God, you have your fruit unto holiness, and the end: everlasting life; VerseEnd Verse23 for the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord. VerseEnd

LEChapter7 Verse1 Do you not know, brethren (for I speak to them that know the law), that the law has dominion over a man only as long as he lives? VerseEnd Verse2 For the woman who has a husband is bound by the law to her husband only as long as he lives; for if the husband is dead, she is released from the law of her husband. VerseEnd Verse3 So then if, while her husband lives, she should be married to another man, she shall be called an adulteress; but if her husband be dead, she is free from that law so that she is no adulteress, though she should be married to another man. VerseEnd Verse4 Wherefore, my brethren, you also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ, that you should be married to another, even to him who is raised from the dead, that we should bring forth fruit unto God. VerseEnd Verse5 For when we were in the flesh, the passions of sins, which were not according to the law, did work in our members to bring forth fruit unto death. VerseEnd Verse6 But now we are delivered from the law wherein we were held, being dead to the law, that we should serve in newness of spirit and not in the oldness of the letter. VerseEnd

Verse7 What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I would not have known sin but by the law; for I would not have known lust except the law had said, You shall not covet. VerseEnd Verse8 But sin, taking opportunity by the commandment, wrought in me all manner of desires. For apart from the law, sin was dead. VerseEnd Verse9 For once I was alive apart from transgression of the law, but when the commandment of Christ came, sin revived and I died. VerseEnd Verse10 And when I believed not the commandment of Christ which came, which was ordained to life, I found it condemned me unto death. VerseEnd Verse11 For sin, taking opportunity, denied the commandment and deceived me, and by it I was slain. VerseEnd Verse12 Nevertheless, I found the law to be holy and the commandment to be holy, and just, and good. VerseEnd Verse13 Was then that which is good made death unto me? God forbid. But sin, that it might appear sin, by that which is good working death in me; that sin, by the commandment, might become exceedingly sinful. VerseEnd

Verse14 For we know that the commandment is spiritual; but when I was under the law, I was yet carnal, sold under sin. VerseEnd Verse15 But now I am spiritual, for that which I am commanded to do, I do, and that which I am commanded not to allow, I allow not. For what I know is not right, I would not do, for that which is sin, I hate. VerseEnd Verse16 If then I do not that which I would not allow, I consent unto the law, that it is good, and I am not condemned. VerseEnd Verse17 Now then, it is no more I that do sin, but I seek to subdue that sin which dwells in me. VerseEnd Verse18 For I know that in me — that is, in my flesh — dwells no good thing; for to desire is present with me, but to perform that which is good, I find not — only in Christ. VerseEnd Verse19 For the good that I would have done when under the law, I find not to be good; therefore, I do it not. But the evil which I would not do under the law, I find to be good; that, I do. VerseEnd

Verse20 Now if I do that, through the assistance of Christ, I would not do under the law, I am not under the law, and it is no more that I seek to do wrong, but to subdue sin that dwells in me. VerseEnd Verse21 I find then that under the law, that when I would do good, evil was present with me. VerseEnd Verse22 For I delight in the law of God after the inward man, VerseEnd Verse23 and now I see another law, even the commandment of Christ, and it is imprinted in my mind; but my members are warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin which is in my members. VerseEnd Verse24 And if I subdue not the sin which is in me, but with the flesh serve the law of sin, oh wretched man that I am. Who shall deliver me from the body of this death? VerseEnd Verse25 I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord then that so with the mind, I myself serve the law of God. VerseEnd

LEChapter8 Verse1 There is therefore now no condemnation to them who are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the spirit. VerseEnd Verse2 For the law of the spirit of life in Christ Jesus has made me free from the law of sin and death. VerseEnd Verse3 For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God, sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh, VerseEnd Verse4 that the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us who walk not after the flesh, but after the spirit. VerseEnd Verse5 For they that are after the flesh do focus on the things of the flesh, but they that are after the spirit, the things of the spirit. VerseEnd Verse6 For to be carnally minded is death, but to be spiritually minded is life and peace, VerseEnd Verse7 because the carnal mind is enmity against God, for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be. VerseEnd Verse8 So then they that are after the flesh cannot please God. VerseEnd Verse9 But you are not after the flesh, but after the spirit, if so be that the spirit of God dwells in you. Now if any man has not the spirit of Christ, he is none of his. VerseEnd Verse10 And if Christ is in you, though the body shall die because of sin, yet the spirit is life because of righteousness. VerseEnd Verse11 And if the spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies by his spirit that dwells in you. VerseEnd

Verse12 Therefore, brethren, we are debtors not to the flesh, to live after the flesh, VerseEnd Verse13 for if you live after the flesh, you shall die unto sin. But if you through the spirit do put to death the deeds of the body, you shall live unto Christ. VerseEnd Verse14 For as many as are led by the spirit of God, they are the sons of God. VerseEnd Verse15 For you have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you have received the spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. VerseEnd Verse16 The spirit itself bears witness with our spirit that we are the children of God. VerseEnd Verse17 And if children, then heirs — heirs of God and joint-heirs with Christ, if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together. VerseEnd Verse18 For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be named with the glory which shall be revealed in us. VerseEnd Verse19 For the earnest expectation of the creation waits for the manifestation of the sons of God, VerseEnd Verse20 for the creation was made subject to tribulation, not willingly, but by reason of him who has subjected it, in hope VerseEnd Verse21 because the creation itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. VerseEnd Verse22 For we know that the whole creation groans and travails in pain together until now. VerseEnd Verse23 And not only they, but ourselves also, who have the firstfruits of the spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, that is, the redemption of our body. VerseEnd

Verse24 For we are saved by hope, but hope that is seen is not hope; for what a man sees, why does he yet hope for? VerseEnd Verse25 But if we hope for that we see not, then with patience we do wait for it. VerseEnd Verse26 Likewise, the spirit also helps our infirmities, for we know not what we should pray for, as we ought. But the spirit itself makes intercession for us with striving which cannot be expressed, VerseEnd Verse27 and he that searches the hearts knows what is the mind of the spirit because he makes intercession for the saints according to the will of God. VerseEnd Verse28 And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose. VerseEnd

Verse29 For him whom he did foreknow, he also did foreordain to be conformed to his own image, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren. VerseEnd Verse30 Moreover, him whom he did foreordain, him he also called; and him whom he called, him he also sanctified; and him whom he sanctified, him he also glorified. VerseEnd

Verse31 What shall we then say to these things? If God is for us, who can prevail against us? VerseEnd Verse32 He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things? VerseEnd Verse33 Who shall lay anything to the charge of God’s elect? It is God that justifies. VerseEnd Verse34 Who is he that condemns? It is Christ who died — yea, rather who is risen again — who is even at the right hand of God, who also makes intercession for us. VerseEnd Verse35 Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? VerseEnd — Verse36 as it is written: For your sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. VerseEnd Verse37 Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors, through him that loved us. VerseEnd Verse38 For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, VerseEnd Verse39 nor height, nor depth, nor any other creation shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord. VerseEnd

LEChapter9 Verse1 I say the truth in Christ; I lie not, my conscience also bearing me witness in the holy ghost, VerseEnd Verse2 that I have great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart. VerseEnd Verse3 For once I could have wished that I were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh, VerseEnd Verse4 who are Israelites — of whom are the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises; VerseEnd Verse5 and are made children unto the fathers; and of whom, as concerning the flesh, Christ was, who is God over all, blessed for ever. Amen. VerseEnd

Verse6 Not as though the word of God has taken no effect, for they are not all Israel who are of Israel. VerseEnd Verse7 Neither because they are all children of Abraham are they the seed, but in Isaac shall your seed be called VerseEnd — Verse8 that is, they who are the children of the flesh are not the children of God, but the children of the promise are counted for the seed. VerseEnd

Verse9 For this is the word of promise: At this time will I come, and Sarah shall have a son. VerseEnd Verse10 And not only Sarah, but when Rebekah also had conceived by one (our father Isaac) VerseEnd — Verse11 for the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand not of works, but of him that calls VerseEnd — Verse12 it was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger. VerseEnd Verse13 As it is written: Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated. VerseEnd

Verse14 What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid. VerseEnd Verse15 For he says to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion. VerseEnd Verse16 So then it is not of him that desires, nor of him that runs, but of God that shows mercy. VerseEnd Verse17 For the scripture says unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised you up, that I might show my power in you, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth. VerseEnd Verse18 Therefore has he mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will, he hardens. VerseEnd

Verse19 You will say then unto me, Why does he yet find fault? For who has resisted his will? VerseEnd Verse20 Nay, but, O man, who are you that replies against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why have you made me thus? VerseEnd Verse21 Has not the potter power over the clay — of the same lump to make one vessel unto honor and another unto dishonor? VerseEnd Verse22 What if God, willing to show his wrath and to make his power known, endured with much long-suffering the vessels of wrath fitted VerseEnd Verse23 to destruction — and that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy whom he had before prepared unto glory, VerseEnd Verse24 even us whom he has called? Not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles? VerseEnd

Verse25 As he says also in Hosea, I will call them my people, who were not my people, and her beloved, who was not beloved. VerseEnd Verse26 And it shall come to pass that in the place where it was said unto them, You are not my people — there shall they be called the children of the living God. VerseEnd

Verse27 Isaiah also cries concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved. VerseEnd Verse28 For he will finish the work and cut it short in righteousness, because a short work will the Lord make upon the earth. VerseEnd Verse29 And as Isaiah said before, Except the Lord of Hosts had left us a seed, we would have been as Sodom, and been made like unto Gomorrah. VerseEnd

Verse30 What shall we say then? That the Gentiles who followed not after righteousness have attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith; VerseEnd Verse31 but Israel, who followed after the law of righteousness, has not attained to the law of righteousness. VerseEnd Verse32 Wherefore, they stumbled at that stumbling stone not by faith, but, as it were, by the works of the law, VerseEnd Verse33 as it is written: Behold, I lay in Zion a stumbling stone and rock of offense, and whoever believes on him shall not be ashamed. VerseEnd

LEChapter10 Verse1 Brethren, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for Israel is that they might be saved. VerseEnd Verse2 For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge; VerseEnd Verse3 for they, being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. VerseEnd Verse4 For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone that believes. VerseEnd

Verse5 For Moses describes the righteousness which is of the law, that the man who does those things shall live by them. VerseEnd Verse6 But the righteousness which is of faith speaks in this way: Say not in your heart, Who shall ascend into Heaven? — that is, to bring Christ down from above. VerseEnd Verse7 Or who shall descend into the deep? — that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead. VerseEnd

Verse8 But what does it say? The word is near you, even in your mouth and in your heart — that is, the word of faith which we preach; VerseEnd Verse9 that if you shall confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus, and shall believe in your heart that God has raised him from the dead, you shall be saved. VerseEnd Verse10 For with the heart man believes unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation. VerseEnd Verse11 For the scripture says, Whoever believes on him shall not be ashamed; VerseEnd Verse12 for there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek, for the same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon him, VerseEnd Verse13 for whoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. VerseEnd

Verse14 How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? And how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? And how shall they hear without a preacher? VerseEnd Verse15 And how shall they preach, except they are sent? — as it is written: How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things! VerseEnd Verse17 So then faith comes by hearing the word of God. VerseEnd

Verse16 But I say, have they not heard? Yes truly, their sound went into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world. But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Isaiah says, Lord, who has believed our report? VerseEnd Verse19 Now I say, did not Israel know? First, Moses says, I will provoke you to jealousy by them who are no people; and by a foolish nation I will anger you. VerseEnd Verse20 But Isaiah is very bold, and says, I was found of them that sought me not; I was made manifest unto them that asked not after me. VerseEnd Verse21 But to Israel he says, All day long I have stretched forth my hands unto a disobedient and obstinate people. VerseEnd

LEChapter11 Verse1 I say then, has God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. VerseEnd Verse2 God has not cast away his people whom he foreknew. Do you not know what the scripture says of Elijah? How he makes complaint to God against Israel, saying, VerseEnd Verse3 Lord, they have killed your prophets and dug down your altars, and I am left alone and they seek my life. VerseEnd Verse4 But what does the answer of God unto him say? I have reserved to myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal. VerseEnd Verse5 Even so then, at this present time also, there is a remnant according to the election of grace. VerseEnd

Verse6 And if by grace, then is it no more of works; otherwise, grace is no more grace. But if it is of works, then it is no more grace; otherwise, work is no more work. VerseEnd Verse7 What then? Israel has not obtained that which they seek for, but the election has obtained it, and the rest were blinded VerseEnd — Verse8 according as it is written: God has given them the spirit of slumber, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear — unto this day. VerseEnd Verse9 And David says, Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumbling block, and a recompense unto them; VerseEnd Verse10 let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back always. VerseEnd

Verse11 I say then, have they stumbled that they should fall? God forbid; but rather through their fall, salvation has come unto the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy. VerseEnd Verse12 Now if the fall of them is the riches of the world, and the diminishing of them the riches of the Gentiles, how much more their fullness? VerseEnd

Verse13 For I speak to you Gentiles: Inasmuch as I am the apostle of the Gentiles, I magnify my office, VerseEnd Verse14 if by any means I may provoke to emulation them who are my flesh and might save some of them. VerseEnd Verse15 For if the casting away of them is the reconciling of the world, what shall the restoring of them be but life from the dead? VerseEnd Verse16 For if the firstfruit is holy, the lump is also holy; and if the root is holy, so are the branches. VerseEnd Verse17 And if some of the branches should be broken off, and you, being a wild olive tree, were grafted in among them, and with them partake of the root and fatness of the olive tree, VerseEnd Verse18 boast not against the branches, for you bear not the root, but the root bears you. VerseEnd Verse19 For if you boast, you will say, The branches were broken off that we might be grafted in. VerseEnd Verse20 Well, because of unbelief they were broken off, and you stand by faith. Be not haughty, but fear, VerseEnd Verse21 for if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not you. VerseEnd Verse22 Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them who fell, severity, but toward you, goodness, if you continue in his goodness; otherwise, you also shall be cut off. VerseEnd

Verse23 And they also, if they continue not still in unbelief, shall be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again. VerseEnd Verse24 For if you were cut out of the olive tree which is wild by nature, and were grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree, how much more shall these, which are the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree? VerseEnd

Verse25 For I desire not, brethren, that you should be ignorant of this mystery, lest you should be wise in your own eyes. That blindness, in part, has happened to Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in. VerseEnd Verse26 Then all Israel shall be saved, as it is written: There shall come out of Zion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob. VerseEnd Verse27 For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins. VerseEnd

Verse28 As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes; but as touching the election, they are beloved for the fathers’ sakes; VerseEnd Verse29 for the gifts and calling of God are unchanged. VerseEnd Verse30 For as you in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief, VerseEnd Verse31 even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy. VerseEnd Verse32 For God has consigned them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all. VerseEnd

Verse33 Oh the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God, how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out! VerseEnd Verse34 For who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been his counselor? VerseEnd Verse35 Or who has first given to him and it shall be recompensed unto him again? VerseEnd Verse36 For of him, and through him, and to him are all things, to whom be glory for ever. Amen. VerseEnd

LEChapter12 Verse1 I implore you, therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God — which is your reasonable service. VerseEnd Verse2 And be not conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, that you may prove what that good, and acceptable, and perfect will of God is. VerseEnd

Verse3 For I say, through the grace given unto me, to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think, but to think soberly, according as God has dealt to every man the measure of faith. VerseEnd Verse4 For as we have many members in one body and all members have not the same office, VerseEnd Verse5 so we, being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another, VerseEnd Verse6 having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us: whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith; VerseEnd Verse7 or ministry, let us wait on our ministering; VerseEnd Verse8 or he that teaches, on teaching; or he that exhorts, on exhortation; he that gives, let him do it with simplicity; he that rules, with diligence; he that shows mercy, with cheerfulness. VerseEnd

Verse9 Love without pretense, and abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good. VerseEnd Verse10 Be kindly disposed one to another with brotherly love, in honor preferring one another, VerseEnd Verse11 not slothful in diligence, fervent in spirit, serving the Lord, VerseEnd Verse12 rejoicing in hope, patient in tribulation, continuing steadfast in prayer, VerseEnd Verse13 distributing to the necessity of saints, given to hospitality. VerseEnd Verse14 Bless them who persecute you — bless, and curse not. VerseEnd Verse15 Rejoice with them that do rejoice and weep with them that weep. VerseEnd Verse16 Be of the same mind one toward another. Regard not high things, but condescend to men of low estate. Be not wise in your own eyes. VerseEnd Verse17 Recompense to no man evil for evil. Provide things good in the sight of all men. VerseEnd Verse18 If it is possible, as much as lies in you, live peaceably with all men. VerseEnd

Verse19 Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath; for it is written: Vengeance is mine, I will repay, says the Lord. VerseEnd Verse20 Therefore, if your enemy hungers, feed him; if he thirsts, give him drink. For in so doing, you shall heap coals of fire on his head. VerseEnd Verse21 Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good. VerseEnd

LEChapter13 Verse1 Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers, for there is no power in the church but of God; the powers that be are ordained of God. VerseEnd Verse2 Whoever therefore resists the power resists the ordinance of God, and they that resist shall receive to themselves punishment. VerseEnd Verse3 For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Do you desire then to not be afraid of the power? Do that which is good and you shall have praise of the same, VerseEnd Verse4 for he is the minister of God to you for good. But if you do that which is evil, be afraid, for he bears not the rod in vain; for he is the minister of God, an avenger to execute wrath upon him that does evil. VerseEnd

Verse5 Wherefore, you must be subject not only for wrath, but also for conscience’s sake. VerseEnd Verse6 For, for this cause you pay your consecrations also unto them. VerseEnd Verse7 But first render to all their dues, according to custom — tribute to whom tribute, custom to whom custom — that your consecrations may be done in fear of him to whom fear belongs, and in honor of him to whom honor belongs. VerseEnd

Verse8 Therefore, owe no man anything but to love one another, for he that loves another has fulfilled the law VerseEnd Verse9 for this: You shall not commit adultery, You shall not kill, You shall not steal, You shall not bear false witness, You shall not covet; and if there is any other commandment, it is briefly comprehended in this saying — namely, You shall love your neighbor as yourself VerseEnd (Verse10 love works no ill to his neighbor; therefore, love is the fulfilling of the law) VerseEnd, Verse11 and that, knowing the time — that now it is high time to awake out of sleep, for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed. VerseEnd

Verse12 The night is far spent, the day is at hand; let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armor of light. VerseEnd Verse13 Let us walk honestly, as in the day, not in rioting and drunkenness, not in bedding and wantonness, not in strife and envying. VerseEnd Verse14 But put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh to gratify the lusts thereof. VerseEnd

LEChapter14 Verse1 Him that is weak in the faith receive, but not to doubtful disputations. VerseEnd Verse2 For one believes that he may eat all things; another, who is weak, eats herbs. VerseEnd Verse3 Let not him that eats despise him that eats not, and let not him who eats not judge him that eats, for God has received him. VerseEnd Verse4 Who are you that judges another man’s servant? To his own master he stands or falls. Yea, he shall be held up, for God is able to make him stand. VerseEnd

Verse5 One man esteems one day above another; another esteems every day alike. Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind. VerseEnd Verse6 He that regards the day, regards it unto the Lord; and he that regards not the day, to the Lord he does not regard it. He that eats, eats to the Lord, for he gives God thanks; and he that eats not, to the Lord he eats not and gives God thanks. VerseEnd

Verse7 For none of us lives to himself, and no man dies to himself; VerseEnd Verse8 for whether we live, we live unto the Lord, and whether we die, we die unto the Lord — whether we live therefore or die, we are the Lord’s. VerseEnd Verse9 For to this end Christ both died, and rose, and revived, that he might be Lord both of the dead and living. VerseEnd

Verse10 But why do you judge your brother? Or why do you set at naught your brother? For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ. VerseEnd Verse11 For I live, says the Lord, and every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall swear to God, as it is written. VerseEnd Verse12 So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God. VerseEnd

Verse13 Let us not therefore judge one another anymore, but judge this rather: that no man put a stumbling block or an occasion to fall in his brother’s way. VerseEnd Verse14 I know, and am persuaded by the Lord Jesus, that there is nothing unclean of itself; but to him that esteems anything to be unclean, to him it is unclean. VerseEnd Verse15 But if your brother is grieved with your food, you walk not charitably if you eat; therefore, destroy not him with your food for whom Christ died. VerseEnd Verse16 Let not then your good be evil spoken of, VerseEnd Verse17 for the kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness, and peace, and joy in the holy ghost. VerseEnd Verse18 For he that in these things serves Christ is acceptable to God and approved of men. VerseEnd

Verse19 Let us therefore follow after the things which aid peace and things with which one may edify another. VerseEnd Verse20 For food, destroy not the work of God. All things indeed are pure, but it is evil for that man who eats with offense. VerseEnd Verse21 It is good neither to eat flesh, nor to drink wine, nor anything whereby your brother stumbles, or is offended, or is made weak. VerseEnd Verse22 Do you have faith? Have it to yourself before God. Happy is he that condemns not himself in that thing which he approves. VerseEnd Verse23 And he that doubts is condemned if he eat, because it is not of faith; for whatever is not of faith is sin. VerseEnd

LEChapter15 Verse1 We then that are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak and not to please ourselves; VerseEnd Verse2 let every one of us please his neighbor for his good to edification. VerseEnd Verse3 For even Christ pleased not himself, but as it is written: The reproaches of them that reproached you fell on me. VerseEnd Verse4 For whatever things were written previously were written for our learning, that we, through patience and comfort of the scriptures, might have hope. VerseEnd Verse5 Now the God of patience and consolation grant you to be like-minded one toward another as was Christ Jesus, VerseEnd Verse6 that you may with one mind and one mouth glorify God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. VerseEnd Verse7 Wherefore, receive one another as Christ also received us to the glory of God. VerseEnd

Verse8 Now I say that Jesus Christ was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of God, to confirm the promises made unto the fathers, VerseEnd Verse9 and that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy, as it is written: For this cause I will confess to you among the Gentiles, and sing unto your name. VerseEnd Verse10 And again he says, Rejoice, you Gentiles, with his people. VerseEnd Verse11 And again, Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and laud him, all you people. VerseEnd Verse12 And again, Isaiah says, There shall be a root of Jesse, and he that shall rise to reign over the Gentiles, in him shall the Gentiles trust. VerseEnd Verse13 Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope through the power of the holy ghost. VerseEnd

Verse14 And I myself also am persuaded of you, my brethren, that you also are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish one another. VerseEnd Verse15 Nevertheless, brethren, I have written the more boldly unto you in some sort as putting you in mind, because of the grace that is given to me of God, VerseEnd Verse16 that I should be the minister of Jesus Christ to the Gentiles, ministering the gospel of God, that the offering up of the Gentiles might be acceptable, being sanctified by the holy ghost. VerseEnd

Verse17 I have therefore whereof I may glory through Jesus Christ, in those things which pertain to God. VerseEnd Verse18 For I will not dare to speak of any of those things which Christ has not wrought by me to make the Gentiles obedient by word and deed, VerseEnd Verse19 through mighty signs and wonders by the power of the spirit of God, so that from Jerusalem and round about unto Illyricum, I have fully preached the gospel of Christ. VerseEnd Verse20 Yea, so have I strived to preach the gospel — not where Christ was named, lest I should build upon another man’s foundation, VerseEnd Verse21 but as it is written: To whom he was not spoken of, they shall see, and they that have not heard shall understand VerseEnd — Verse22 for which cause also I have been much hindered from coming to you. VerseEnd

Verse23 But now, having no more place in these parts, and having a great desire these many years to come unto you, VerseEnd Verse24 whenever I take my journey into Spain, I will come to you; for I trust to see you in my journey, and to be brought on my way there by you, if first I am somewhat filled through your prayers. VerseEnd Verse25 But now I go unto Jerusalem to minister unto the saints, VerseEnd Verse26 for it has pleased them of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor saints who are at Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse27 It has pleased them, and their debtors they are; for if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister unto them in carnal things. VerseEnd Verse28 When therefore I have performed this, and have sealed to them this fruit, I will come by you into Spain. VerseEnd Verse29 And I am sure that, when I come unto you, I shall come in the fullness of the blessing of the gospel of Christ. VerseEnd

Verse30 Now I implore you, brethren, for the Lord Jesus Christ’s sake and for the love of the spirit, that you strive together with me in your prayers to God for me, VerseEnd Verse31 that I may be delivered from them that do not believe in Judea, and that my service which I have for Jerusalem may be accepted of the saints, VerseEnd Verse32 that I may come unto you with joy by the will of God, and may with you be refreshed. VerseEnd Verse33 Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen. VerseEnd

LEChapter16 Verse1 I commend unto you Phoebe our sister, who is a servant of the church which is at Cenchrea, VerseEnd Verse2 that you receive her in the Lord as becomes saints, and that you assist her in whatever business she has need of you; for she has been a succorer of many, and of myself also. VerseEnd Verse3 Greet Priscilla and Aquila, my helpers in Christ Jesus, VerseEnd Verse4 who have for my life laid down their own necks, unto whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles; VerseEnd Verse5 likewise, greet the church that is in their house. Salute my well-beloved Epaenetus, who is the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ. VerseEnd Verse6 Greet Mary, who expended much labor on us. VerseEnd Verse7 Salute Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen and my fellow prisoners, who are of note among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me. VerseEnd Verse8 Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord. VerseEnd Verse9 Salute Urbanus, our helper in Christ, and Stachys, my beloved. VerseEnd Verse10 Salute Apelles, approved in Christ. Salute those who are of Aristobulus’ church. VerseEnd Verse11 Salute Herodion, my kinsman. Greet those that are of the church of Narcissus, who are in the Lord. VerseEnd Verse12 Salute Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Salute the beloved Persis, who labored much in the Lord. VerseEnd Verse13 Salute Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine. VerseEnd Verse14 Salute Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brethren who are with them. VerseEnd Verse15 Salute Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints who are with them. VerseEnd Verse16 Salute one another with a holy salutation. The churches of Christ salute you. VerseEnd

Verse17 Now I implore you, brethren, mark those who cause divisions and offenses contrary to the doctrine which you have learned, and avoid them; VerseEnd Verse18 for they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly, and by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple. VerseEnd Verse19 For your obedience has come abroad unto all men. I am glad therefore on your behalf, but yet I would have you wise unto that which is good, and simple concerning evil. VerseEnd Verse20 And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen. VerseEnd

Verse21 Timothy (my fellow worker), and Lucius, and Jason, and Sosipater (my kinsmen) salute you. VerseEnd Verse22 I, Tertius, who wrote this epistle, salute you in the Lord. VerseEnd Verse23 Gaius (my host — and the whole church) salutes you. Erastus (the chamberlain of the city) salutes you, and Quartus, a brother. VerseEnd Verse24 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen. VerseEnd

Verse25 Now to him that is of power to establish you, according to the gospel and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery which was kept secret since the world began VerseEnd Verse26 but now is made manifest, and by the scriptures of the prophets, according to the commandment of the everlasting God, made known to all nations for the obedience of faith VerseEnd — Verse27 to God only, wise, be glory through Jesus Christ for ever. Amen. VerseEnd

p.i: Written to the Romans from Corinth, and sent by Phoebe, servant of the church at Cenchrea.
